why: Inserting the Order Principle to keep quotative/report phrases attached shifted many cut decisions to avoid splitting those phrases, moving several top cut positions (big change at rank‑1, gains at ranks 2–4). The effect is a small net improvement concentrated in bins that retain many candidate cuts (≤7–10 pieces), while cases that relied on the original top‑1 cut were slightly harmed.
lesson: When adding quotative‑attachment, avoid altering the primary (rank‑1) cut choice that long‑latency budgets depend on; ensure the rule adjusts deeper candidate positions without wholesale replacement of the top cut.
